Is `GetDatumMemSize` not need to export? Could we rename it to `getDatumMemSize`?

I just want to reuse `GetDatumMemSize` in func_group_concat_test.go, so expose it. Rename it to `getDatumMemSize` and write same method in func_group_concat_test.go will be better?

ok, you need to add a comment for it to resolve following error.
```
[2020-09-29T08:38:31.415Z] linting
[2020-09-29T08:38:31.981Z]   ✘  https://revive.run/r#exported  exported function GetDatumMemSize should have comment or be unexported  
[2020-09-29T08:38:31.981Z]   executor/aggfuncs/func_group_concat.go:555:1
```
please keep this blank line
there are multi args, we need to check `IsNull` for every args
It's ok in the current situation, but I think every column should be checked more rigorously.
if the `buffer` is not nil, we should add an `e.sep` to `buffer`
ok
`sortRow.byItems` had append a lot of Datums which are add to the `p.topN` finally. should we need to evaluate the memory usage of it also? @b41sh @William0423
I agree, we should add the size of row
Should we evaluate the memDelta according to the Datum's type?
Ok, I will add memory usage of Datums.

@William0423 @b41sh
I think we need to calculate the `memDelta` in the `tryToAdd` which has `heap.push`, `heap.pop` and `buffer.Truncate` operations that will affect the memory usage. What your opinions?

@mmyj 
I think `memDelta - the memory usage of heap.Pop(h) ` shall be calculated. `currSize` has calculated memory changes for   `buffer.Truncate`. `heap.Push(h, row)` seems have no effect on `memDelta`.
I agree, IMO we could write the memdelta calculated logic in the tryToAdd function.
yes, we can return `memDelta` in the `tryToAdd` function.
ok
can we use argvs[0] as `ByItems`? like `aggfuncTest`, so that we can remove `[]* util.ByItems`.

If we have a table `t` and `GROUP_CONCAT( b,c order by c, b)` as follow, `argvs[0]` is  `column b`, `ByItems` include  `column b, c`. It seens that `[]* util.ByItems `must be used as a function parameter if we want to calculate `Datums` memory size.
`create table t(a bigint, b bigint, c bigint);`
`select GROUP_CONCAT( b,c order by c, b) from t ;`
